scenario.prompt_to_agent:
A user reboots their PC and now cannot get an IP address. Other
PCs that were already up keep working (their existing leases are
still valid). Newly connected devices on any internal VLAN time
out waiting for DHCP. Existing TCP sessions are unaffected.
Diagnose.
scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: r1 dhcpd (ISC DHCP server)
Mechanism: r1 is the central DHCP server for every internal
  VLAN (A-PC, A-Phone, A-Mgmt, B-PC, B-Phone, B-Mgmt, Wi-Fi).
  DSWs relay DHCPDISCOVER as unicast to 10.0.0.76 (R1's
  loopback). With dhcpd dead, requests reach r1 but get no
  reply. Existing leases keep working until their lifetime
  expires; renewals start failing after lease-time/2.
Localization: r1
Root cause: dhcpd is not running on r1
Fix: restart dhcpd — `/etc/init.d/isc-dhcp-server restart`
  on r1 (or however the lab launches dhcpd)
scenario.fix_spec:
restart dhcpd — `/etc/init.d/isc-dhcp-server restart`
  on r1 (or however the lab launches dhcpd)

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: Central DHCP server (isc-dhcp-server) on router r1. The distribution switches are running DHCP relay, but the DHCP server process itself is down.

Mechanism: New clients broadcast DHCPDISCOVER on their VLANs; the distribution switches relay these to the configured server IP 10.0.0.76 (r1 loopback). Because isc-dhcp-server on r1 is not running and nothing is listening on UDP/67, no DHCPOFFER/ACK packets are returned. Existing hosts keep working because they already have valid leases and active sessions don’t immediately require renewal.

Localization: 
- Relays are up: dswa1 and dswb1 show dhcrelay listening on UDP/67 and are configured to forward to 10.0.0.76; they can ping 10.0.0.76 successfully.
- Server is down: On r1, systemctl shows isc-dhcp-server is inactive (dead), and netstat shows no UDP/67 listener (only dhclient on UDP/68). The DHCP configuration exists at /etc/dhcp/dhcpd.conf with pools for all internal VLANs, confirming r1 is the intended server.

Root cause: The isc-dhcp-server service on r1 is stopped/inactive, leaving no DHCP responder for relayed requests.

Corrective fix: Start and enable the DHCP service on r1 (e.g., systemctl start isc-dhcp-server; systemctl enable isc-dhcp-server). Verify it binds to UDP/67 and begins answering relayed requests. Review r1’s logs (journalctl -u isc-dhcp-server) for the reason it was down to prevent recurrence. No L2/L3 forwarding changes are needed; the relay and routing paths are healthy.

per_axis.rationale: The diagnosis explicitly identifies r1 as the affected device, stating the isc-dhcp-server on r1 is inactive/dead.
Agent explicitly identifies the ISC DHCP server (isc-dhcp-server/dhcpd) on r1 as the affected component.
The report explicitly states existing hosts keep working on their valid leases while new DHCPDISCOVERs receive no offers, thus distinguishing existing vs. new leases.
Recommends starting/enabling the isc-dhcp-server on r1 and verifying UDP/67 binding, which matches the expected restart/remediation.

The investigation log explicitly shows dhcrelay running on distribution switches pointing at 10.0.0.76, connectivity to 10.0.0.76 is good, and isc-dhcp-server on r1 is inactive; the agent’s conclusions follow directly and the recommended fix is appropriate.
